overview.title: Overview
overview.text: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga, located near the holy city of Dwarka in Gujarat, is one of the 12 revered Jyotirlinga shrines. The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva as the 'Lord of Serpents' and is believed to offer protection from all forms of poison, negativity, and evil.

mythology.title: Mythological Origin
mythology.text: The legend tells of a demon named Daruka who imprisoned a Shiva devotee named Supriya. Supriya chanted the Shiva mantra 'Om Namah Shivaya' relentlessly. Pleased, Lord Shiva appeared, vanquished the demon, and resided here in the form of a Jyotirlinga, taking the name Nageshwar.

architecture.title: Architectural Highlights
points: The current temple is a modern reconstruction, built with pink stone.
The most prominent feature is the giant 82-foot-tall seated statue of Lord Shiva in a meditative pose.
The main sanctum (garbhagriha) is located underground.
The architecture is simple and elegant, designed to accommodate a large number of devotees.
A large pond is located near the temple, adding to the serene atmosphere.

significance.title: Spiritual Significance
points: Worshipping at Nageshwar is believed to neutralize the effects of all poisons, both physical and spiritual.
It is considered a powerful place for protection against negative energies and evil forces.
The location near Dwarka, the kingdom of Lord Krishna, marks a significant confluence of Shaivism and Vaishnavism.

events.event: The site's origin is detailed in the Shiva Purana.
The present temple structure and the giant Shiva statue were built and funded by the T-Series music label owner, Gulshan Kumar.

items.text: A darshan here is believed to grant a poison-free and fearless life.
The temple is considered a powerful center for devotees suffering from 'Sarpa Dosha' (astrological affliction related to serpents).

conclusion.title: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Nageshwar Jyotirlinga offers a unique spiritual experience, highlighted by its powerful legend of protection and the magnificent, calming statue of Lord Shiva. It stands as a modern pilgrimage center built upon an ancient foundation of faith.

aboutPostCards.title: Major Festivals
items: Maha Shivratri – The main festival, celebrated with special pujas and a large fair.
Nag Panchami – An important day to worship the 'Lord of Serpents'.

aboutPostCards.title: Nearby Attractions
items: Dwarkadhish Temple – One of the Char Dham sites, dedicated to Lord Krishna.
Bet Dwarka – An island believed to be the original residence of Lord Krishna.
Gopi Talav – A pond associated with the Gopis of Vrindavan.
Rukmini Devi Temple – A temple dedicated to Lord Krishna's chief consort.

methods.title: By Road
methods.description: Nageshwar is about 17 km from Dwarka city. Dwarka is well-connected by road to major cities in Gujarat.

methods.title: Nearest Railway
methods.description: Dwarka Railway Station (DWK) is the nearest railhead.

methods.title: Nearest Airport
methods.description: Jamnagar Airport (JGA) is the closest, approximately 137 km away.
